title: The Second Part, or A Continuance of Poly-Olbion, from the Eighteenth Song
author: Michael Drayton
reason: The thirtieth Song is a verse chorography of Westmorland and Cumberland, taking the Muse over Kendal, up Skiddaw and through Copland to the Derwent lakes.

title: Britannia: or, A Chorographical Description of Great Britain and Ireland, Volume 2
author: William Camden
reason: Gibson's enlarged English Britannia devotes self-contained county chapters to Cumberland and Westmorland, describing Winandermere, Derwentwater and Skiddaw.

title: A Tour thro' the Whole Island of Great Britain, Volume 3
author: Daniel Defoe
reason: Letter X of this volume carries Defoe north through Kendal into Westmorland and Cumberland, with his famous account of the barren, frightful mountain country.

title: A Description of the Lake at Keswick, and the Adjacent Country, in Cumberland
author: John Brown
reason: Brown's short letter on Derwentwater is the founding text of Lake District picturesque description, praising Keswick's beauty, horror and immensity.

title: A Six Months Tour through the North of England, Volume 3
author: Arthur Young
reason: This volume runs from Carlisle to Kendal with a sustained section on Winandermere and the Westmorland lakes alongside agricultural and manufacturing notes.

title: An Excursion to the Lakes in Westmoreland and Cumberland, August 1773
author: William Hutchinson
reason: An entire early tour narrative of the Lakes, describing Windermere, Coniston, Derwentwater and Ullswater day by day.

title: The Antiquities of Furness; or, An Account of the Royal Abbey of St Mary in the Vale of Nightshade
author: Thomas West
reason: West's antiquarian survey of Furness, the south-western district of the Lakes, covering the abbey, Coniston and the Furness fells.

title: The History and Antiquities of the Counties of Westmorland and Cumberland, Volume 2
author: Joseph Nicolson and Richard Burn
reason: The standard eighteenth-century county history of the two Lakeland counties, with parish-by-parish accounts of Keswick, Grasmere, Windermere and the lake valleys.

title: A Guide to the Lakes: Dedicated to the Lovers of Landscape Studies
author: Thomas West
reason: The first true Lake District guidebook, organising the region into stations and viewpoints and shaping tourist practice for half a century.

title: The Works of Thomas Gray
author: Thomas Gray
reason: Includes Gray's celebrated 1769 Journal of his tour in the Lakes, the day-by-day Keswick, Borrowdale and Grasmere account that shaped Lakeland taste.

title: A Survey of the Lakes of Cumberland, Westmorland, and Lancashire
author: James Clarke
reason: Clarke's large survey by a local land surveyor gives measured, anecdotal accounts of every lake, with tenures, customs and folklore.

title: The Poetical Works of Miss Susanna Blamire, the Muse of Cumberland
author: Susanna Blamire
reason: Collects the Cumberland dialect songs and pastoral verse of a native Cumberland poet, with a section of Songs in the Cumberland Dialect.

title: Remarks Made in a Tour from London to the Lakes of Westmoreland and Cumberland
author: Adam Walker
reason: A letter-form tour wholly directed at the Westmorland and Cumberland lakes by a native of the district.

title: The History of the County of Cumberland, and Some Places Adjacent, Volume 1
author: William Hutchinson
reason: A major county history of Cumberland including extended topographical accounts of Keswick, Borrowdale and the Derwent lakes.

title: Observations, Relative Chiefly to Picturesque Beauty, Made in the Year 1772, on Several Parts of England, Particularly the Mountains and Lakes of Cumberland and Westmoreland
author: William Gilpin
reason: Gilpin's Lakes tour is the central statement of picturesque aesthetics applied to Cumberland and Westmorland scenery.

title: A Fortnight's Ramble to the Lakes in Westmorland, Lancashire, and Cumberland
author: Joseph Budworth
reason: A lively pedestrian tour of the Lakes, including the ascent of Skiddaw and the Langdale and Coniston valleys.

title: Windermere, a Poem
author: Joseph Budworth
reason: A poem wholly devoted to Windermere and its shores, with topographical notes on the lake.

title: A Journey Made in the Summer of 1794 ... To Which Are Added Observations During a Tour to the Lakes of Lancashire, Westmoreland, and Cumberland, Volume 2
author: Ann Radcliffe
reason: The second volume contains Radcliffe's self-contained Lakes tour, with sublime descriptions of Windermere, Derwentwater and Skiddaw.

title: A Companion, and Useful Guide to the Beauties of Scotland, To the Lakes of Westmoreland, Cumberland, and Lancashire
author: Sarah Murray
reason: A practical guide by a woman traveller with a dedicated section on routes, inns and views throughout the English Lakes.

title: A Descriptive Tour, and Guide to the Lakes, Caves, Mountains, and Other Natural Curiosities in Cumberland, Westmoreland, Lancashire
author: John Housman
reason: A Cumberland-born writer's complete guide to the lakes, caves and mountains of the district.

title: Through England on a Side Saddle in the Time of William and Mary
author: Celia Fiennes
reason: Fiennes's 1698 riding journal includes a northern stage through Kendal, Windermere and Ullswater, the earliest woman's eyewitness account of the Lakes.

title: An Excursion to the Highlands of Scotland and the English Lakes
author: Joseph Mawman
reason: The return leg of this tour is a sustained account of the English Lakes with literary and topographical recollections.

title: Letters from England: by Don Manuel Alvarez Espriella, Volume 2
author: Robert Southey
reason: Southey's fictive Spanish traveller devotes a run of letters to Keswick and the surrounding lakes, where Southey himself lived.

title: Ballads in the Cumberland Dialect
author: Robert Anderson
reason: The Cumberland Bard's ballads are the classic verse record of Lakeland rural speech, fairs, weddings and manners.

title: The Tourist's New Guide, Containing a Description of the Lakes, Mountains, and Scenery in Cumberland, Westmorland, and Lancashire, Volume 1
author: William Green
reason: Green lived at Ambleside and wrote the most detailed artist's guide to the lakes, fells and valleys of the district.

title: Oakwood Hall, a Novel; Including a Description of the Lakes of Cumberland and Westmorland, Volume 1
author: Catherine Hutton
reason: A novel whose plot is built around a touring party's progress through the Cumberland and Westmorland lakes.

title: Tours to the British Mountains, with the Descriptive Poems of Lowther, and Emont Vale
author: Thomas Wilkinson
reason: Wilkinson, a Quaker of Yanwath near Penrith, records walking tours of the Lakeland fells together with poems on Lowther and the Eamont.

title: The Remains of John Briggs: Containing Letters from the Lakes, Westmorland as It Was, and Other Tales
author: John Briggs
reason: The Letters from the Lakes and Westmorland as It Was record local life, customs and landscape by a Westmorland-born journalist.

title: A Concise Description of the English Lakes, and Adjacent Mountains
author: Jonathan Otley
reason: Otley was the first to describe the geological structure of the Lakes; his pocket guide combines topography, heights and rock strata.

title: A Guide through the District of the Lakes in the North of England
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's prose guide is the defining account of Lake District landscape, its inhabitants and the effects of tourism.

title: A Complete Guide to the Lakes, Comprising Minute Directions for the Tourist, with Mr Wordsworth's Description of the Scenery and Three Letters on the Geology by Professor Sedgwick
author: John Hudson and Adam Sedgwick
reason: Combines a Kendal tourist guide with Wordsworth's description and Sedgwick's pioneering letters on Lake District geology.

title: The Recreations of Christopher North, Volume 1
author: John Wilson
reason: Wilson wrote from Elleray on Windermere; these essays include extended Lakeland sporting, angling and mountain sketches.

title: Kendal and Windermere Railway: Two Letters Re-printed from the Morning Post
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's public protest against extending the railway into the Lakes, a founding document of Lake District conservation.

title: The Scenery and Poetry of the English Lakes: A Summer Ramble
author: Charles Mackay
reason: A summer tour of the Lakes interleaving landscape description with the poetry associated with each place.

title: The Prelude, or, Growth of a Poet's Mind: An Autobiographical Poem
author: William Wordsworth
reason: The poem's opening books are a sustained imaginative record of a Cumberland and Westmorland boyhood among the lakes and fells.

title: Rides on Railways Leading to the Lake and Mountain Districts of Cumberland, the Peak of Derbyshire, the Dales of Derbyshire
author: Samuel Sidney
reason: A railway-age tourist handbook whose principal section directs excursionists to Windermere, Keswick and the Cumberland mountains.

title: Tales and Legends of the English Lakes and Mountains
author: Wilson Armistead
reason: A collection of legends attached to specific Lake District valleys, lakes and fells.

title: Black's Picturesque Guide to the English Lakes, Including an Essay on the Geology of the District
author: Adam and Charles Black
reason: One of the best-selling Victorian Lakes guides, combining routes, scenery and a geological essay on the district.

title: A Complete Guide to the English Lakes
author: Harriet Martineau
reason: Written from Martineau's home at Ambleside, this guide treats the district's scenery, society and economy at length.

title: The Angler in the Lake District; or, Piscatory Colloquies and Fishing Excursions in Westmoreland and Cumberland
author: John Davy
reason: Colloquies and excursions devoted to the fish, rivers and lakes of Westmorland and Cumberland.

title: Round the Sofa, Volume 2
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
reason: Contains the novella Half a Life-Time Ago, set entirely on the fell farms of the moorland between Kendal and Coniston.

title: The History and Topography of the Counties of Cumberland and Westmoreland
author: William Whellan
reason: A comprehensive directory-history of the two Lakeland counties, parish by parish.

title: Recollections of the Lakes and the Lake Poets: Coleridge, Wordsworth, and Southey
author: Thomas De Quincey
reason: De Quincey's memoir of his Grasmere years and of the Lake Poets in their Lakeland setting.

title: The Lake Country
author: Eliza Lynn Linton
reason: A Cumberland-born writer's district-by-district account of Lake Country landscape, customs and traditions.

title: The Ferns of the English Lake Country, with a List of Varieties
author: William James Linton
reason: A botanical survey of the ferns of the Lake District, written and illustrated at Brantwood, Coniston.

title: The Songs and Ballads of Cumberland, to Which Are Added the Best Poems in the Dialect
author: Sidney Gilpin
reason: An anthology gathering the song and ballad tradition of Cumberland and the Lake Country.

title: Lizzie Lorton of Greyrigg, Volume 1
author: Eliza Lynn Linton
reason: A novel set in a Cumberland fellside parish, drawing on the author's Lake District upbringing.

title: Handbook for Travellers in Westmorland, Cumberland, and the Lakes
author: John Murray
reason: Murray's authoritative handbook covering every route, pass and lake in the district.

title: On the Drifts of the West and South Borders of the Lake District, and on the Three Great Glacial Periods
author: Daniel Mackintosh
reason: A glacial-geological study of the borders of the Lake District and the evidence for successive ice periods.

title: The Glaciation of the Northern Part of the Lake District
author: James Clifton Ward
reason: A Geological Survey officer's detailed account of glacial action in the northern Lake District fells.

title: Lays and Legends of the English Lake Country, with Copious Notes
author: John Pagen White
reason: Ballads and legends localised to named Lakeland valleys, tarns and crags, with antiquarian notes.

title: Cumbriana; or, Fragments of Cumbrian Life
author: William Dickinson
reason: A Cumbrian farmer's record of Lakeland agricultural life, sports, dialect and customs.

title: The Geology of the Northern Part of the English Lake District
author: James Clifton Ward and Robert Etheridge
reason: The official Geological Survey memoir for the northern Lake District, covering the Skiddaw Slates and Borrowdale Volcanics.

title: A Protest against the Extension of Railways in the Lake District
author: Robert Somervell
reason: A campaigning pamphlet, with a preface by Ruskin, against railway schemes in the Lake District.

title: Autobiography, with Memorials by Maria Weston Chapman, Volume 2
author: Harriet Martineau
reason: Covers Martineau's years at The Knoll, Ambleside, with accounts of Lakeland neighbours, building and society.

title: The English Lake District as Interpreted in the Poems of Wordsworth
author: William Angus Knight
reason: Identifies and describes the Lake District places named or implied throughout Wordsworth's poetry.

title: Lakeland: A Descriptive Poem in Four Cantos
author: John Smyth
reason: A long descriptive poem taking the Lake District's lakes and mountains as its whole subject.

title: The Thorough Guide to the English Lake District
author: Mountford John Byrde Baddeley
reason: The standard late-Victorian walkers' and climbers' guide to the Lake District, route by route.

title: Pre-historic Remains in the Lake District: A Paper Read before the Keswick Literary and Scientific Society
author: W. Kinsey Dover
reason: A survey of stone circles, cairns and prehistoric remains within the Lake District.

title: Sonnets at the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: A sonnet sequence written on Lake District places by the Keswick vicar and National Trust founder.

title: The Lazy Tour of Two Idle Apprentices
author: Charles Dickens and Wilkie Collins
reason: The opening chapters are a sustained comic account of the ascent of Carrock Fell in Cumberland and of Hesket Newmarket and Wigton.

title: A Flora of the English Lake District
author: John Gilbert Baker
reason: A systematic botanical flora covering the whole of the English Lake District.

title: Hortus Inclusus: Messages from the Wood to the Garden, Sent in Happy Days to the Sister Ladies of the Thwaite, Coniston
author: John Ruskin
reason: Ruskin's letters from Brantwood on Coniston Water to his Coniston neighbours, full of local weather, lake and fell observation.

title: Leaves from the Annals of a Mountain Parish in Lakeland: Being a Sketch of the History of Torver
author: Thomas Ellwood
reason: A parish history of Torver in the Coniston fells, with Norse place-names and local customs.

title: Robert Elsmere, Volume 1
author: Mary Augusta Ward
reason: The first book is set wholly in Long Whindale, a fictionalised Westmorland dale, with extended Lake District landscape writing.

title: A History of Cumberland
author: Richard Saul Ferguson
reason: A scholarly county history of Cumberland, covering the Lakeland dales, Keswick and Derwentwater.

title: Beneath Helvellyn's Shade: Notes and Sketches in the Valley of Wythburn
author: Samuel Barber
reason: A book-length study of the Wythburn valley under Helvellyn, recorded as Thirlmere was being turned into a reservoir.

title: A Vertebrate Fauna of Lakeland, Including Cumberland and Westmorland with Lancashire North of the Sands
author: Hugh Alexander Macpherson
reason: The standard faunal survey of the Lake District counties, recording birds, mammals, reptiles and fish.

title: Thorstein of the Mere: A Saga of the Northmen in Lakeland
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: A saga-style novel of Norse settlement set on Coniston Water and the surrounding Lakeland fells.

title: Rock-Climbing in the English Lake District
author: Owen Glynne Jones
reason: The foundational Lake District rock-climbing guide, describing routes on Scafell, Pillar Rock and Great Gable.

title: The Geology of the Country between Appleby, Ullswater, and Haweswater
author: John Roche Dakyns and Richard Hill Tiddeman
reason: Geological Survey memoir for the eastern Lake District around Ullswater and Haweswater.

title: Lakeland Words: A Collection of Dialect Words and Phrases as Used in Cumberland and Westmorland
author: Bryham Kirkby
reason: A glossary and set of dialect sketches recording the spoken language of the Lake District.

title: A Thousand Miles of Wandering along the Roman Wall, the Old Border Region, Lakeland, and Ribblesdale
author: Edmund Bogg
reason: A long walking tour with an extended self-contained Lakeland section covering the central fells and dales.

title: Notes on the Early Sculptured Crosses, Shrines and Monuments in the Present Diocese of Carlisle
author: William Slater Calverley
reason: A detailed record of pre-Conquest crosses and monuments across Cumberland and the Lake District parishes.

title: Life and Nature at the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Essays on Lake District seasons, wildlife, farming and folk life by the Keswick vicar and National Trust founder.

title: Coniston Tales
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: Stories rooted in the history, legends and landscape of Coniston and the southern Lake District.

title: Holidays in the English Lakeland: What to See in This World-Famous Holiday Country
author: William Thomas Palmer
reason: A turn-of-the-century tourist account of the Lake District's valleys, passes and peaks.

title: Journals of Dorothy Wordsworth, Volume 1
author: Dorothy Wordsworth
reason: The Alfoxden and Grasmere journals record daily life, weather and walking in the Lake District between 1800 and 1803.

title: Letters of Samuel Taylor Coleridge, Volume 1
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
reason: A long run of letters written from Greta Hall, Keswick, including the celebrated descent of Scafell and accounts of Grasmere and Skiddaw.

title: Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends
author: John Keats
reason: Contains the self-contained sequence of letters from the 1818 northern walking tour describing Windermere, Ambleside, Helvellyn and Skiddaw.
